Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). Consolidated findings F8, F22, F24, F25, F26, F27, F42.

Headline (F8): the most likely first-contact failure produces the exact signature the tool defines as "the run crashed". Verified against a scratch repo: mix spec.check --root <repo-with-no-.spec> exits 1 with a bare RuntimeError stack trace on stderr and NOTHING on stdout. Preflight passes (git, base, project all fine), then Index.detect_spec_dir/1 raises at lib/ancora/index.ex:64 and Output.gated classifies :internal at output.ex:215 and re-raises with no verdict. Ancora.Output.read_protocol/0 tells every agent and CI consumer that a non-zero exit with no verdict line means the gate crashed. So the ordinary state of a repo that has not yet run mix spec.init is indistinguishable from a tool defect. A missing git binary takes the same path (System.cmd raises :enoent at git.ex:26; preflight only matches ok/error at preflight.ex:32-42), and spec.status behaves identically, breaking its own always-exit-0 requirement.
Fix: add a missing-corpus check to Preflight.run/2 returning {:env, "no .spec/ directory in <root>; run mix spec.init"}; wrap System.cmd("git", ...) so :enoent becomes {:error, :git_executable_not_found} the way BatchPort already does; map {:cat_file_batch_exited, _} and :cat_file_batch_timeout to {:env, _}. Widen ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails to name the new conditions, which its own Intent prose already claims. Decide and write down the rule for unreadable files: four call sites crash and three degrade.

F22 — give run_after_preflight/2 an explicit case mapping RunContext.start/3 failures to {:env, message}, naming the missing-git case. gate.ex:36 has an else-less with that lets {:error, _} escape past Gate.check own @spec, surfacing as "ungated return from {:error, :git_executable_not_found}".
F27 — stop discarding git captured output in Preflight.git_repo/1 and resolve_base/3; distinguish exit 128 from other statuses and include the real error text.
F24 — make a failed fetch/3 poison the batch port: close it, mark it dead, return {:error, :port_poisoned} from later calls, so a silent wrong blob becomes a loud failure. Add a test forcing a 0ms timeout that asserts the next fetch does not return the stale record.
F25 — after Port.close/1, wait for {port, {:exit_status, _}} with a bounded timeout instead of the 500ms port-monitor guess; replace TmpGitRepo.cleanup!/1 Process.sleep(30) with a bounded poll.
F26 — derive.ex:146 collect_resolution({:exit, reason}, _) is unreachable: Task.async_stream links to a caller that does not trap exits, so a raising resolver kills the gate outright and the after blocks do not run (verified empirically; this is the mechanism behind the temp-dir leak). Either trap exits so the clause becomes real, or delete it — and add a test that makes the resolver raise.
F42 — remove BaseView.blobs/3 nil default, or add a clause returning a real error for it.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails and the env tier in test/ancora/gate_test.exs and subprocess tests in test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs and test/mix/tasks/spec_status_test.exs; test/ancora/git_test.exs and test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs for :enoent and port poisoning; test/ancora/derive/pipeline_test.exs for a raising resolver; test/ancora/base_view_test.exs for the blobs/3 nil clause
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) mix spec.check --root <repo-with-no-.spec> prints a tier=env line naming mix spec.init and a verdict, exit per the env tier, nothing on stderr but the diagnostic; (2) a missing git binary takes the same path; (3) spec.status keeps its own exit contract on both; (4) run_after_preflight/2 maps every RunContext.start/3 failure to {:env, message}; (5) preflight captures and surfaces git's real error text and distinguishes exit 128; (6) a failed fetch/3 poisons the batch port and the next fetch returns {:error, :port_poisoned}, never a stale record (0ms timeout test); (7) Port.close waits on exit_status with a bounded timeout and TmpGitRepo.cleanup!/1 polls instead of sleeping; (8) a raising resolver either surfaces through a real collect_resolution clause or that clause is deleted, with a test that makes the resolver raise and asserts temp dirs are cleaned; (9) the unreadable-file rule is written down in ancora.gate and the four crashing sites follow it
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: a missing corpus, missing git, or dead port ends in a tier=env verdict line, never a bare stack trace.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex, lib/ancora/index.ex (detect_spec_dir), lib/ancora/output.ex (env classification only)
- lib/ancora/git.ex, lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex, lib/ancora/base_view.ex
- lib/ancora/derive.ex, lib/ancora/derive/run_context.ex, lib/ancora/status.ex
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (widen preflight_hard_fails and write the unreadable-file rule; substantive)
- .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md (acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement/scenario updates that clear drift/growth/shrink for this ticket's own changes; never weakening a must)
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, correcting an admission defect: this list allowed lib/ancora/derive.ex, lib/ancora/base_view.ex and lib/ancora/status.ex but not the subject specs that govern them, so the drift those edits raise could not be cleared. Acknowledgment edits only, on the same terms as ancora.tasks above)
- .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state.md (same correction: the governance co-change gate forces a decision-record edit when the charter's own claims move)

- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/**
- lib/ancora/parser.ex
- lib/ancora/verifier.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/** beyond what the env path needs

Out of Scope (intent):
- no shallow-clone detection (ancora-11w lands on top of this)
- no --json shape redesign (ancora-xla.5); the env payload may gain the message only if a test already pins it
- no base-tree narrowing (ancora-xla.3)

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

  chmod 000 lib/sample.ex, HEAD: exit 1, stdout EMPTY, stderr "ungated return from {:error, {:source_read, \"lib/sample.ex\", :eacces}}". Base: also a crash, "gate assembly failed: {:source_read, ...}" raised from gate.ex:115. So the lib case is unfixed rather than regressed.
The regression is real and it is the one that matters: readable_tag_files/2 at gate.ex:287 intercepts a finding the base reported correctly and converts it into a verdict-less RuntimeError. The added spec clause is written, has no scenario and no test, and the code contradicts it. Ticket verification item (9) is not met.

Gap 2 assessment: Bounce, bundled into this one. It is not a no-behaviour hunk, so the "Note, not a bounce" materiality rule does not reach it. I measured it myself rather than taking the verifier's numbers: 20 samples of open, one fetch, close in each tree against the same fixture. HEAD c3aaa97 min 10.178 ms, max 30.660 ms, mean 11.584 ms. Base 7511407 min 0.025 ms, max 1.732 ms, mean 0.126 ms. Every HEAD sample sits at or above the 10 ms @close_timeout, so the receive at lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:111 always expires. Port.close/1 terminates the port synchronously and never sends {port, {:exit_status, _}} to the owner, so the wait the spec describes cannot succeed. The base's :erlang.monitor(:port, port) DOWN message did arrive, which is why the base returned in microseconds under a 500 ms bound. The completion record's "500.7 ms per call across 20 samples before and 14.7 ms after" does not reproduce in either direction; close/1 got roughly 90x slower, not 34x faster. That measurement claim should be withdrawn from the record. Nothing hangs, so this is small, but the epic already bounced ancora-v1n for a spec statement false at HEAD and this is the same class.

Verifier assessment: Correct on both Gaps, and correct in its supporting detail. Not over-read and not under-read on anything I checked. Its mechanical counts match the diff exactly at 20 files, 0 outside the corrected Allowed globs, 0 Out-of-Scope, no Spec-Ack trailer. Its gate reading matches mine. Its Notes are right too: preflight ordering putting git before corpus is harmless, and the deleted collect_resolution({:exit, reason}, _) clause turning an externally killed task into a FunctionClauseError is advisory given timeout: :infinity. The one seam, System.put_env on PATH in test/ancora/git_test.exs forcing async: false, is the only seam in the diff and it does not hide a disconnected production path: the second test drives the real Ancora.Gate.Preflight.run/2, and the verifier separately proved the same condition through a real mix subprocess. The FAIL was the right call.

Bounce reason:

Gap 1 is a CODE fix. The spec clause is already correct; leave it as written. Make assemble/5's error reach gate_error/1 in lib/ancora/gate.ex. The smallest change that does it is to stop calling assemble/5 from the with body in run/3, so its return is matched rather than passed through. Keep the try/after File.rm_rf(base_root) exactly as it is, capture its result, and case on it:

  {:ok, report} -> {:ok, report}
  {:error, reason} -> gate_error(reason)

alongside the existing else that already routes ChangeSet.compute/1 and BaseView.materialize/1 failures to gate_error/1. No memo, no registry, no new process, no new module. gate_error({:source_read, path, reason}) at gate.ex:397 already produces the right {:env, "cannot read <path>: <reason>"} message, so nothing new is needed there.
Then add the proving test, which the diff currently lacks entirely. A subprocess test in test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs tagged ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails: create_project + write_anchored_subject, chmod 0o000 the tagged test file, assert the last stdout line is "spec.check result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0", assert stdout names the file, and refute result.stderr =~ "RuntimeError". Repeat for lib/sample.ex, which is the unfixed-not-regressed half. Restore the mode in on_exit, and guard the test so it skips when running as root, where chmod 000 does not deny reads. Add a matching scenario to .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md covering ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails, since the three scenarios added by this diff cover missing corpus, missing git and the poisoned port but nothing covers the unreadable-file clause.

Gap 2 is a SPEC fix, with a code revert I recommend alongside it. Delete the sentence "Closing a port shall wait for its exit status with a bounded timeout." from ancora.derive.base_reads_batched in .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md. Do not try to make the code satisfy it; Port.close/1 cannot deliver that message, so any attempt adds machinery to chase behaviour that does not exist. The other clauses added to that requirement block are true and should stay. Separately, restore close/1 in lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex to the :erlang.monitor(:port, port) form it had at 7511407, including the demonitor with :flush, and drop @close_timeout. That is a revert, not an addition, and it returns close/1 to microseconds. If you would rather not revert, then delete the receive block outright, since Port.close/1 is already synchronous and drain_port_messages/1 is what actually matters. Either way the false sentence goes.
Also correct the completion record: the 500.7 ms before / 14.7 ms after figures are not reproducible and the real direction is the opposite.
